messages:
cheng: FYI — after the 03:00 kube-operator rollout a subset of us-west-2 nodes started rejecting GPU workloads. Pods are Pending with `NodeAffinity` fallbacks kicking in. :eyes:
cheng: kubectl describe pod shows:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age                From               Message
  ----     ------             ----               ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   2m (x6 over 5m)    default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 4 node(s) had taint {gpu-driver-mismatch: true}, 8 node(s) didn't match GPU resource requests.
```
cheng: `nvidia-device-plugin` on those nodes is advertising CUDA 12.2 while host driver reports 12.1. Device plugin probe is advertising capabilities before driver probe completes apparently.
sam: I saw similar on staging last week after we bumped the gpu-operator to v1.6. The deviceplugin pod now probes `/var/lib/nvidia` earlier which can surface advertised version mismatch.
irene: ops-bot shows these nodes were updated with kernel 5.15.0-102 and a driver hotpatch. Might be a timing/order issue between kernel/drv module load and device-plugin startup.
ops-bot: DeployRolloutBot: rollout gpu-operator v1.6 started at 2024-06-12T03:00Z. 22 nodes targeted. 5 nodes upgraded so far.
mike: quick check — are we seeing NCCL complaints or just scheduling? Any loss in running pods?
cheng: so far RN jobs are fine because they're on nodes with older driver. This affected queued/burst jobs which landed on freshly-upgraded nodes. No NCCL errors in running pods yet.
sam: short term workaround: mark the upgraded nodes with a label `gpu-ready=false` to avoid scheduling new GPU jobs until we confirm driver/deviceplugin ordering. Command: `kubectl label node <node> gpu-ready=false --overwrite`
irene: we also can tweak the device-plugin DaemonSet to add `initContainers` that wait for `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` to exist before advertising. Something like:
```
initContainers:
- name: wait-for-driver
  image: busybox
  command: ['sh','-c','until [ -f /proc/driver/nvidia/version ]; do sleep 1; done']
```
sam: that'd prevent the premature advertise but is a bit of a bandaid. Long term we should ensure driver install completes before kubelet uncordons or before device-plugin starts. Maybe reorder the node upgrade job.
mike: one constraint: us-west-2 currently at quota for spare GPUs so draining and reprovisioning elsewhere is not trivial. If we over-label nodes we risk backing up the queue and impacting PLG experiments — cost vs latency tradeoff.
cheng: agreed. Proposal: 1) label the 5 nodes `gpu-ready=false` (short-term), 2) patch device-plugin with initContainer (medium), 3) reconfigure upgrade job to wait for driver module and do a staged uncordon (long). I'll open a follow-up runbook PR.
irene: +1. Also add a monitoring alert on device-plugin version vs driver version mismatch per node (diff metric) so ops gets paged before scheduling problems.
sam: I can push the label change now and roll the initContainer as a canary in staging.
ops-bot: Action logged: cheng assigned to runbook PR; sam will patch DS canary.
cheng: thanks — I'll create a short incident note and tag infra-oncall. :thumbsup:
